methodological_rigor.justification: Single-institution retrospective cohort of 215 patients with NCCN-defined VHR or regional prostate cancer treated with HDR-BT + EBRT + ADT over 17 years, with a median follow-up of 5.6 years (up to 17.3). Consistent institutional protocol but three sequential HDR-BT/EBRT regimens with similar BEDs introduce heterogeneity acknowledged by the authors. Analytical approach (Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression, Phoenix criteria for biochemical failure, CTCAE v5.0 for toxicity) is standard and appropriate for the question; however, only 19 recurrences and 4 PC-specific deaths limit statistical power for multivariable modeling and create risk of overfitting with several covariates. No external validation, propensity matching, or competing-risk analysis for OS given high non-cancer mortality.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual retrospective cohort (Oxford 2b) of a relatively large VHR/regional PC population treated with a modern multimodal regimen. Findings support HDR-BT + EBRT + ADT as an effective option and identify pre-RT PSA >0.1 ng/mL and cT4 as independent predictors of recurrence, which could inform patient counseling and systemic intensification decisions. Translational impact is meaningful but not practice-changing in the absence of randomized or multicenter confirmation, particularly with emerging treatment-intensification trial data.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational cohort reporting is generally competent with clear description of cohort selection, treatment protocols over three eras, toxicity using CTCAE v5.0, and Kaplan-Meier/Cox outputs with 95% CIs. STROBE checklist is not explicitly cited and no participant flow diagram is provided for the 574-to-215 selection. Ethics approval and consent are not discussed in the provided text. No data or code sharing statement; quality-of-life outcomes not analyzed.

novelty_literature.justification: Authors position this as the first study evaluating HDR-BT outcomes specifically in the updated NCCN VHR and regional categories, which is a meaningful incremental contribution situated among prior Japanese retrospective studies using older risk classifications (Kasahara, Mori, Makino et al.). The underlying treatment approach and the identified prognostic factors (PSA, T stage) are well-established; the novelty is primarily in restratifying outcomes under the new NCCN definition rather than introducing a new intervention or biomarker.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written and well organized with logical flow from background through methods, results, and a thoughtful discussion that contextualizes findings against alternative modalities (RP, SBRT) and ongoing intensification trials (DASL-HiCaP, ATLAS, PEACE-2, ALADDIN). Tables, figures, and protocol evolution are clearly described. Limitations section is notably candid about retrospective design, evolving techniques, stage migration with mpMRI/PSMA-PET, low event counts, and absence of quality-of-life endpoints.

key_strengths: First application of updated NCCN VHR/regional criteria to a HDR-BT + EBRT + ADT cohort with 17-year follow-up (median 5.6 years)
Large single-institution cohort of 215 patients with consistent institutional workflow and modern dose-escalation regimens (BED ~233-241 Gy)
Favorable 5-year and 8-year RFS/CSS/OS outcomes with very low Grade 3+ toxicity (1.9% GU, 0% GI) in an aggressive disease population
Identification of pre-RT PSA >0.1 ng/mL and cT4 as independent prognostic factors with direct implications for risk-adapted intensification
Thorough and candid limitations acknowledging stage migration, evolving protocols, low event numbers, and lack of QoL data
key_concerns: Retrospective single-institution, single-ethnicity (Japanese) design with potential selection bias and limited generalizability
Only 19 recurrences and 4 PC-specific deaths limit multivariable power; competing-risks analysis for OS not performed despite non-cancer-dominated mortality
Treatment regimen heterogeneity across three eras (2006-2014, 2014-2022, 2022-) introduces residual confounding not formally adjusted
No data sharing, no STROBE checklist, and no explicit participant flow diagram for 574-to-215 cohort selection
No comparison with contemporary EBRT-alone or SBRT-boost controls; imaging staging heterogeneity with variable PSMA-PET availability
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid real-world single-institution evidence with long follow-up for HDR-BT + EBRT + ADT in updated NCCN VHR/regional PC, appropriate for a Tier 3 oncology journal pending minor revisions to address reporting, event-number caveats, and competing risks.
